value.text:
Wayne's brother, and nobody's afterthought.

Michael Wilson broke in with the Ravens, made his name with the Vikings and finished as a Titan. He took over in Minnesota the season after injury ended Sherman Brandson's career, and the dynasty never blinked: five rings in six seasons, throwing to God Johnson, who set the career receiving record in those years.

He was a pocket passer in the purest sense: 413 rushing yards in his entire career, because he never needed to run. He completed 72 percent of his passes over 214 games for 58,992 yards and 690 touchdowns, more than three touchdown passes a game. The one exception was near the goal line, where he kept it himself and scored 36 rushing touchdowns on only 101 carries.

Six MVPs. Six rings, the last of them in Tennessee, before injury cut his final season short. Wayne's name rested on durability; Michael's rests on all of it. Michael Wilson, welcome to the Hall of Fame.
